editorial:
Imagine stepping into the secret world of the Edo period harem, where everything looks pretty but feels dangerous. You follow two new girls trying to survive the mean girls and scary politics of the palace. The vibe is very trippy and colorful, almost like a living painting. Then, a mysterious medicine seller shows up. He is the only one who can see the ghost causing all the trouble. It feels like a detective story mixed with a ghost story, and the art style will definitely keep you glued to your screen because it is unlike anything you have seen before.

The pacing is great and the mystery keeps you guessing until the very end. You will love how the medicine seller breaks down the ghost's secrets, though some of the political drama might feel a bit slow at first. It is a perfect pick if you like weird art and spooky mysteries. Just make sure you have a big screen to really enjoy the visuals.
endingExplained: The medicine seller finds out the spirit is fueled by the sadness and anger of the women in the harem. He reveals the truth about the betrayal and the hidden pain that created the monster. Once the truth is out in the open, the spirit is finally calmed and disappears. The girls learn to trust each other, and the medicine seller moves on to his next adventure, leaving the palace in peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves unique art styles and ghost mysteries.
